I am 39 years old, and I have only been farming on my own for three years, so I still follow what the older farmers in my village do. My family has four mouths to feed, and some of us work off-farm when construction jobs come up, so I cannot spend all day in the fields. With just 5 mu of land and a well for irrigation, I need to keep things simple, reliable, and not too costly.

For winter wheat, I will plant improved seed — probably something like Shimai or Liangxing, which my neighbors use and which I can get cheaply at the local shop. I will rotary till the field before sowing, because that is what everyone here does. I will put down compound fertilizer as a basal dose and then topdress with urea. I am not precise with the numbers, but I know the bag sizes, and I will use roughly what my uncle uses: about 25 jin of nitrogen fertilizer and 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. That should give the wheat enough food. I will irrigate three times — once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at jointing, and once at heading or filling — because the well water is not free but three times is enough to get a decent crop. I will spray pesticides about four times over the season for weeds, insects, and disease. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For summer maize, I plant right after the wheat harvest. There is no time to waste, so I will not till the soil — I will plant directly into the wheat stubble. I must use hybrid seed, like Nongda or Denghai; everyone says the yield is much better than old varieties. I will apply a starter compound fertilizer at sowing and maybe some urea later if the plants look yellow. I will irrigate twice — once after sowing to help germination, and once during the big growth period or before grain filling. I will spray pesticides three times to control weeds and the borers that always show up. I hope for about 550 kg per mu.
